properties.name: AMBIENT_BRIGHTNESS
properties.comment:
this controls the brightness of the final calculated ambient term that this shader calculates
NOTE: this does not affect direct lighting

properties.name: FINAL_BRIGHTNESS
properties.comment: this controls the brightness of the final combined ambient + direct light that this shader ultimately returns

properties.name: CAMERA_AMBIENT_LIGHT
properties.comment:
calculates a fresh direct lighting term for a "light source" that is placed right where the camera is (capcom style)
this lighs up the diffuse/specular terms in ambient areas

properties.name: CAMERA_AMBIENT_LIGHT_RANGE
properties.comment: how far out the camera light reaches (in (cm) units)

properties.name: CAMERA_AMBIENT_LIGHT_BRIGHTNESS
properties.comment: how bright the camera light is (affects diffuse and specular)

properties.name: CAMERA_AMBIENT_LIGHT_SPECULAR_BOOST
properties.comment: how bright the camera light specular contribution is (affects specular only)

properties.name: DISABLE_IRRADIANCE
properties.comment: (DEBUG) disables the final global illumination irradiance/diffuse shading term

properties.name: IRRADIANCE_BLENDING_DEFAULT
properties.comment:
this is the default diffuse/irradiance global illumination the game does.
they sample the regular baked GI irradiance volumes, and then also try to use the "cubemap reflections" resampling them for "irradiance" and combine the two together
cool idea in theory... but doesn't really work that well in practice mostly because the cubemap reflection volumes they have scattered throughout the game world are really sparse
not to mention in many areas this combination of the irradiance volume and the reflection probes leads to a loss of color and some accuracy, contrast is better though but ehh I think it's better to just sample the irradiance volume directly
NOTE TO SELF: to improve on their original idea I think we should calculate an "influence distance" since technically the closer we get to a reflection probe the more accurate the irradiance is at that point (more so than the irradiance volume)

properties.name: FLATTEN_CHARACTER_AMBIENT
properties.comment:
this makes it so skin/eye/hair materials on characters only sample from the irradiance volume rather than all the other shenangins
this flattens out their face in ambient light, but good occlusion will take care of shading them and occluding details for the most part
plus... I think everyone prefers them looking flat rather than bug-eyed in ambient light
the downside is less contrast/shading on their face, and even less color in certain spots, but generally overall this improves their faces during gameplay significantly.
far less of a "frog face" look.

properties.name: SSAO_POWER
properties.comment:
controls how strong the AO term is in ambient light (use in tandem with SSAO_BRIGHTNESS)
NOTE: original game SSAO is much weaker than the SSGI AO, if your flipping back and fourth you'll need to readjust the values
Higher Values: more contrast
Lower Values: less contrast

properties.name: SSAO_BRIGHTNESS
properties.comment:
controls how bright the AO term is in ambient light (use in tandem with SSAO_POWER)
NOTE: original game SSAO is much weaker than the SSGI AO, if your flipping back and fourth you'll need to readjust the values
Higher Values: brighter
Lower Values: darker

properties.name: RANDOM_ANIMATE_NOISE
properties.comment: (SSGI) changes the noise pattern every frame for the new SSGI / AO (HIGHLY recomended, so the TAA in the game natrually blends results)

properties.name: SSGI_RAY_COUNT
properties.comment:
how many SSGI/AO rays we fire
IMPORTANT NOTE: this settings is insanely expensive, if you want to send your GPU to heaven in the name of less noise and better quality... be my geust!

properties.name: SSGI_RAYMARCHING_STEP_COUNT
properties.comment:
how many raymarching samples we do
higher samples = better quality / less noise / worse performance
lower samples = worse quality / more noise / better performance

properties.name: SSGI_RAYMARCHING_WIDTH
properties.comment:
how far out does the SSGI max screen-pixel reach
NOTE: affects both the SSGI AO and bounce light

properties.name: SSGI_THICKNESS
properties.comment:
world-space depth thickness
NOTE: affects both the SSGI AO and bounce light
this controls how thick occluders are in the scene (since there is no way to properly determine the actual thickness of objects, we have to assume a generalized thickness)

properties.name: SSGI_NORMAL_BIAS
properties.comment: how much the SSGI/AO ray is pushed away from the surface it originates from to prevent self-occlusion

properties.name: SSGI_NORMAL_BIAS_HAIR
properties.comment: (for HAIR materials) how much the SSGI/AO ray is pushed away from the surface it originates from to prevent self-occlusion

properties.name: AO_HAIR
properties.comment: control over how strong AO is for hair materials for SSAO/SSGI

properties.name: SSGI_AMBIENT_OCCLUSION
properties.comment:
calculate ground truth visibility based ambient occlusion
this heavier than the original games SSAO, but it's far higher quality
the added bonus is that this sets up alot of infrastructure for the bounce light

properties.name: SSGI_BOUNCE_LIGHT
properties.comment:
calculate bounce light portion for SSGI pass, reusing the same information as the ambient occlusion
this dramatically improves the lighting quality. adding bounce light from the sun, catching emissives or materials in the games that previously were not emitting light
this DOES impact performance quite a bit, needing to sample the color buffer in order to bounce light around
and also in its current state, there is no filtering so this can contribute to quite a bit noise in the final image

properties.name: SSGI_CHECKERBOARD
properties.comment:
shade half of the expensive SSGI rays each frame and reconstruct the missing half from the two computed neighbors in the same 2x2 pixel quad
NOTE: checkerboard rendering is a definite WIN for performance especially at high resolutions, I think it's wise to leave this on even at the expense of quality

properties.name: SSGI_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION
properties.comment: (SSGI_CHECKERBOARD ONLY) reconstruct the missing half of the checkerboard SSGI rays from the two computed neighbors in the same 2x2 pixel quad

properties.name: SSGI_BASIC_QUAD_DENOISE
properties.comment:
A very small sample-free denoise pass that averages the SSGI bounce-light color
across all four pixels in the current 2x2 quad.
NOTE: this only filters SSGI color; ambient occlusion and the fallback mask are untouched.
NOTE 2: personally I would not use this, this is just a last-ditch cheap effort to help somewhat mitigate the noise, in the future this will be replaced by a proper filter pass but for now can somewhat help.

properties.name: DISABLE_RADIANCE
properties.comment: (DEBUG) disables the final global illumination radiance/reflection shading term

properties.name: DISABLE_SSR
properties.comment:
this disables SSR blending and instead fully relies on the reflection probes / irradiance volume the game uses for reflections
NOTE: this does not give you a performance boost, SSR pass still runs, it just wont be used (if you do want a boost, find the SSR pass hlsl file and there is also a disable macro written there)

properties.name: CORRECT_REFLECTION_DIRECTION
properties.comment: this corrects the original strange stretched reflection vectors

properties.name: RADIANCE_BLENDING_DEFAULT
properties.comment:
this is the default reflection/radiance global illumination the game does.
they sample the regular baked GI irradiance volumes, and try to blend them with the "cubemap reflections" to combine the two together
cool idea in theory... but doesn't really work that well in practice mostly because the cubemap reflection volumes they have scattered throughout the game world are really sparse
not to mention in many areas this combination of the irradiance volume and the reflection probes leads to a loss of color and some accuracy, contrast is better though but ehh I think it's better to just sample the radiance volume directly
NOTE TO SELF: to improve on their original idea I think we should calculate an "influence distance" since technically the closer we get to a reflection probe the more accurate the irradiance is at that point (more so than the irradiance volume)

properties.name: RADIANCE_CUBEMAP_MAX_SATURATION
properties.comment:
maximum amount of cubemap chromaticity allowed to replace the radiance-volume color
0.0 keeps reflections fully radiance tinted; 1.0 permits the original cubemap chromaticity

properties.name: RADIANCE_CUBEMAP_MAX_SATURATION_ROUGHNESS
properties.comment: maximum roughness that still receives RADIANCE_CUBEMAP_MAX_SATURATION

properties.name: RADIANCE_CUBEMAP_FULL_RADIANCE_TINT_ROUGHNESS
properties.comment:
minimum roughness at which the cubemap is fully tinted by the radiance-volume color
roughness values between the two thresholds smoothly reduce cubemap chromaticity

properties.name: RADIANCE_SPECULAR_HIGHLIGHT_FORCE_VOLUME_TINT
properties.comment:
radianceVolume.a contains the SampleGI-derived specular-highlight mask
highlighted pixels force the reflection chromaticity back to the radiance-volume color

properties.name: RADIANCE_SPECULAR_HIGHLIGHT_VOLUME_TINT_STRENGTH
properties.comment: strength of the radianceVolume.a chromaticity override

properties.name: SSR_CONTRIBUTION_MULTIPLIER
properties.comment:
controls how much of the SSR is visible
higher values = SSR more visible
lower vlaues = SSR less visible
default is at 100000 (why? because I modified the SSR shader and now its way higher quality. reflection quality is better + way less specular leaks... and plus the original game reflection cubemaps are really ugly and bad. SSR is the only hope of retaining some dignity for good quality reflections)

properties.name: SPECULAR_OCCLUSION_DIRECT_LIGHT_SHADOW
properties.comment:
this is an artistic tweak that darkens only rough cubemap-based reflections (not SSR reflections)
this is because a significant amount of specular/light leak comes from these imprecise reflection sources
so to mitigate that we go in and use the direct light buffer (which already has all direct light shading) and effectively derive a "non direct light" mask
using that mask we darken rough reflections that are not in direct light of anything

properties.name: SPECULAR_OCCLUSION_DIRECT_LIGHT_SHADOW_FACTOR
properties.comment: how much do we darken the original cubemap reflections when they are not in direct light

properties.name: SPECULAR_EYE_HIGHLIGHT
properties.comment: this is mostly artistic, but this adds an additional highlight for character eyes that comes from the camera to give them an extra specular kick

properties.name: SPECULAR_EYE_HIGHLIGHT_BOOST
properties.comment: how intense the specular highlight is for character eyes

properties.name: DEFAULT_GAME_SHADING
properties.comment:
by default it appears that the irradiance volume data is basically ambient cube
it's efficent but not the best quality and has it's problems
but we can project those irradiance coefficents into SH to get the data in spherical harmonics.

properties.name: SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_IRRADIANCE_ZH3
properties.comment:
in plain english: this is more accurate, and leads to less contrast
technical yapping: this evaluates the converted spherical harmonics "irradiance/diffuse" global illumination term using zonal harmonics
where the coefficents we reconstructed are effectively order 2, but with zonal harmonics we can "hallucinate" a 3rd order leading to less ringing

properties.name: CHARACTER_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_SHADING
properties.comment:
this uses the dominant direction of baked global illumination to help give extra shading/contrast to characters when in ambient light (half-lambert)
this is not physically accurate at all, just purely an artistic effect

properties.name: CHARACTER_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_SHADING_AMOUNT
properties.comment: when CHARACTER_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_SHADING is active, this controlshow strong the contrast is for character materials when in ambient light (half-lambert)

properties.name: SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE
properties.comment:
this is an experimental feature, that uses the dominant direction and treats it like a light source to get additional shading/contrast in ambient areas.
it also uses contact shadows to help give a more grounded look to the shading, and to help mitigate some of the shortcomings of baked global illumination
this is not physically accurate at all, this is purely just an artistic effect.

properties.name: RANDOM_ANIMATE_NOISE
properties.comment:
(CONTACT SHADOWS) this changes the noise pattern every frame, which with Temporal Anti-Aliasing (or DLSS or anything related)
you want to do, that way samples change every frame and results get blended together over time for a better final apperance

properties.name: ENABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
calculates contact shadows for dominant direction of ambient light
in short it raymarches against the scene depth buffer to estimate shadows
significantly improves overall shadow quality

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_SAMPLES
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this directly controls the quality of the contact shadows, the more the better!
HIGHER VALUES: better quality shadows, less noise (more stable), and denser but expensive performance
LOWER VALUES: lower quality shadows, more noise (less stable), and lighter but cheaper performance

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_RAY_LENGTH
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this controls how far out the shadows go in screen space (and also can make shadows appear darker/denser or lighter depending on sample count)
HIGHER VALUES: shadows can reach farther, but can become noiser, and more expensive (more screen area)
LOWER VALUES: shadows don't reach as far, but can become more stable, and cheaper (less screen area)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_THICKNESS
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this controls how "thick" objects are in the depth buffer
HIGHER VALUES: larger volume of shadow, but can lead to alot of wierd false shadowing. objects up close can cast shadows onto objects far behind it which can look odd.
LOWER VALUES: smaller volume of shadow, less false shadowing, but they can appear less dense and might be too thin

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_BIAS
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_BIAS_HAIR
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces for hair specifically
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_NORMAL_BIAS
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces using surface normal
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_EARLY_SKY_OUT
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
OPTIMIZATION: this avoids calculating contact shadows for sky pixels
has no effect visually, but can save you quite a bit of frametime especially the more you look up :P
honestly no reason you should turn this off unless you want to suffer in vain...

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
OPTIMIZATION: this calculates contact shadows for every other pixel in a checkerboard like pattern that switches every frame
it saves a small bit of frametime, but does have a quality degredation with more visible shimmering at distances
disable if you want sharper true per-pixel contact shadows (at a bit of a perf hit)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
[CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD ONLY!] This only works if checkerboarding is enabled!
this tries to fill in the gaps intelligently during checkerboard rendering minimize holes where no shadow is calculated

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION_TYPE_MIN
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
[CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD and CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION ONLY!] This only works if checkerboarding and quad reconstruction is enabled!
sharper | checks within the 2x2 checker block and if there is a shadow pixel it just copies it

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION_TYPE_AVG
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
smoother | takes the values within the 2x2 checker block and averages them together for a slightly softer apperance

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_STRENGTH
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this was requested by quite a few people who wanted to control the strength of the shadows
physical accuracy is at 1.0 full power, and natrually global illumination (ambient, bounce, transmission light) fills in shadows
however the games GI term is far from perfect and can leave some areas quite dark so here you can control it
reduction in shadow strength can create an odd 90s style look where you can see a semblance of light leaking through to "fill in" for the shadow.
not a fan of it, and it's not accurate, but hey to each their own!

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_DEFAULT_LIT
properties.comment: (SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_CLOTH
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this does get used on characters but it's not common, default_lit

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_PREINTEGRATED_SKIN
properties.comment: (SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_SUBSURFACE_PROFILE
properties.comment: (SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_HAIR
properties.comment: (SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_EYE
properties.comment: (SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_FALLOFF
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
another requested feature...
this is an added effect that will gradually "fade" contact shadows as it goes further out
this does have a bit of a perf hit with (extra instructions per iteration in the loop now)
I've done my best to optimize and keep it light, but it just requires more instructions to achieve
still, in the grand scheme of things this should be pretty light and enabled if you really want to mitigate some of shortcomings (atleast its not another texture sample)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_FALLOFF_CONTRAST
properties.comment:
(SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_DIFFUSE ONLY)
this shapes the falloff
higher values = sharper/darker shadow further out
lower values = softer/lighter shadow further out

properties.name: CORRECT_REFLECTION_DIRECTION
properties.comment: game doing a stretched reflection vector based on roughness for some reason? it looks ugly and wrong

properties.name: SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_SPECULAR_HIGHLIGHT
properties.comment:
derrive a specular highlight based on the dominant direction of ambient light
this helps give specular materials a very nice and plausible/accurate kick of reflection that is based on the baked ambient global illumination
I HIGHLY recomend keeping this on

properties.name: SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_SPECULAR_HIGHLIGHT_DUAL
properties.comment:
for an extra "artistic" specular kick we can calculate another specular highlight but coming from the opposite dominant direction
this can help give an extra shine in areas of shadow or facing away from the main dominant direction

properties.name: CAMERA_VIEW_SPECULAR_HIGHLIGHT
properties.comment:
derrive a specular highlight from the camera
this is more artistic admittedly, and is not entirely accurate/plausible unless there is a light at camera
with that said this also like the dominant SH specular highlight gives a very nice kick to the reflection term for the baked ambient global illumination

properties.name: SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_SPECULAR_OCCLUSION
properties.comment: calculate a specular occlusion term (half lambert) that darkens reflections on the dominant direction of ambient light

properties.name: SPHERICAL_HARMONICS_DOMINANT_DIRECTION_SPECULAR_OCCLUSION_FACTOR
properties.comment: controls how strong the specular occlusion term is, higher values darken reflections facing away from the dominant direction of ambient light

properties.name: TONEMAP_GRAN_TURISMO_7_SDR_PAPER_WHITE
properties.comment: defines the SDR reference white level used in our tone mapping (typically 250 nits). cd/m^2

properties.name: TONEMAP_REINHARD2_WHITE
properties.comment: white point for the reinhard 2 tonemapper

properties.name: TONE_MAPPING_UCS_ICTCP
properties.comment: Mode options.

properties.name: SHADING_DEFAULT_LIT_LAMBERT
properties.comment:
this is the original shading model used for the game
its simple, and efficent, but not accurate
if you want to retain the original game shading turn this on

properties.name: SHADING_DEFAULT_LIT_BURLEY
properties.comment:
new shading model, little different but more accurate to diffuse shading in real life
visually it makes diffuse materials more "diffuse" and matte as it should caused by retro-reflection (when you look away from the light direction)
but for some artistically this might be undesirable

properties.name: SHADING_DEFAULT_LIT_OREN_NAYAR
properties.comment:
new shading model, little different but more accurate to diffuse shading in real life
similar to burley, visually it makes diffuse materials more "diffuse" and matte as it should caused by retro-reflection (when you look away from the light direction)
but for some artistically this might be undesirable

properties.name: ENABLE_MICRO_SHADOWS
properties.comment:
simulates micro-level shadowing on materials (using material ao) super cheap and performant! (from uncharted 4)
but this can lead to some materials/objects looking much darker than usual.
if this is not desired you can just disable to revert to (mostly) original shading

properties.name: ENABLE_MICRO_SHADOWS_SKIN
properties.comment:
applies microshadows to skin, generally shadowing terms should be mostly unified, however this can lead to an overly dark appearance characters in certain conditions and areas
I would leave it off if you desire characters to stay true to their original game shading

properties.name: ENABLE_MICRO_SHADOWS_HAIR
properties.comment:
applies microshadows to hair, generally shadowing terms should be mostly unified, however this can lead to an overly dark appearance characters in certain conditions and areas
I would leave it off if you desire characters to stay true to their original game shading

properties.name: MICRO_SHADOWS_STRENGTH
properties.comment:
requested feature for control over strength of shadows, the uncharted 4 micro shadow application at full intensity can be quite strong
leaving some places a little too dark when in direct sunlight, but here you have control over how strong it is

properties.name: APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT
properties.comment:
apply SSAO to the direct lighting for more contrast
NOTE: I don't recomend this, as it's not only physically in-accurate, but can create too much "shadowing" for things that are supposed to be in direct light
but... it's here if you prefer the look

properties.name: SSAO_POWER
properties.comment:
[APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT ONLY!] This only works if APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT is enabled!
this controls the "contrast" of the SSAO term when applied to direct light

properties.name: SSAO_BRIGHTNESS
properties.comment:
[APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT ONLY!] This only works if APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT is enabled!
this controls the "brightness" of the SSAO term when applied to direct light, I suggest using this in tandem with SSAO_POWER

properties.name: RANDOM_ANIMATE_NOISE
properties.comment:
this changes the noise pattern every frame, which with Temporal Anti-Aliasing (or DLSS or anything related)
you want to do, that way samples change every frame and results get blended together over time for a better final apperance

properties.name: RANDOM_INTERLEAVED_GRADIENT_NOISE
properties.comment:
less "noisy" pattern, more stable and slightly better performing
NOTE 1: for animated noise, I recomend this as it's more stable

properties.name: RANDOM_BLUE_NOISE
properties.comment:
more "noisy" pattern, less stable and slightly worse perfoming
NOTE 1: for NON-animated noise, I recomend using this (because it's sample pattern has better distribution across a single frame)
NOTE 2: game uses this by default

properties.name: ENABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS
properties.comment:
the main attraction, contact shadows!
in short it raymarches against the scene depth buffer to estimate shadows
significantly improves overall shadow quality

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_SAMPLES
properties.comment:
this directly controls the quality of the contact shadows, the more the better!
HIGHER VALUES: better quality shadows, less noise (more stable), and denser but expensive performance
LOWER VALUES: lower quality shadows, more noise (less stable), and lighter but cheaper performance

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_RAY_LENGTH
properties.comment:
this controls how far out the shadows go in screen space (and also can make shadows appear darker/denser or lighter depending on sample count)
HIGHER VALUES: shadows can reach farther, but can become noiser, and more expensive (more screen area)
LOWER VALUES: shadows don't reach as far, but can become more stable, and cheaper (less screen area)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_IMPROVED_THICKNESS
properties.comment: use a more accurate thickness hueristic that grows with the projected pixel footprint of the occluder, instead of a constant thickness for every sample

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_THICKNESS
properties.comment:
maximum assumed view-space thickness of an occluder.
with the improved path, the actual thickness starts at CONTACT_SHADOWS_MIN_THICKNESS and grows with the projected pixel footprint up to this cap.
with the legacy path this is the constant thickness used for every sample.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_MIN_THICKNESS
properties.comment: minimum thickness value of an occluder

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_PIXEL_THICKNESS_SCALE
properties.comment: multiplier for the view-space size of one pixel at the sampled depth.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_SELF_OCCLUSION_SKIP_STEPS
properties.comment:
receiver exclusion in march steps.
this prevents the first tested depth interval from overlapping the surface that launched the ray.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_GRAZING_EXTRA_SKIP_STEPS
properties.comment: extra exclusion at grazing light angles, where the ray remains close to the receiver plane for longer.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_BIAS
properties.comment:
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_BIAS_HAIR
properties.comment:
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces for hair specifically
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_NORMAL_BIAS
properties.comment:
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces using surface normal
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_EARLY_SKY_OUT
properties.comment:
OPTIMIZATION: this avoids calculating contact shadows for sky pixels
has no effect visually, but can save you quite a bit of frametime especially the more you look up :P
honestly no reason you should turn this off unless you want to suffer in vain...

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD
properties.comment:
OPTIMIZATION: this calculates contact shadows for every other pixel in a checkerboard like pattern that switches every frame
it saves a small bit of frametime, but does have a quality degredation with more visible shimmering at distances
disable if you want sharper true per-pixel contact shadows (at a bit of a perf hit)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION
properties.comment:
[CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD ONLY!] This only works if checkerboarding is enabled!
this tries to fill in the gaps intelligently during checkerboard rendering minimize holes where no shadow is calculated

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION_TYPE_MIN
properties.comment:
[CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD and CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION ONLY!] This only works if checkerboarding and quad reconstruction is enabled!
sharper | checks within the 2x2 checker block and if there is a shadow pixel it just copies it

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION_TYPE_AVG
properties.comment: smoother | takes the values within the 2x2 checker block and averages them together for a slightly softer apperance

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_STRENGTH
properties.comment:
this was requested by quite a few people who wanted to control the strength of the shadows
physical accuracy is at 1.0 full power, and natrually global illumination (ambient, bounce, transmission light) fills in shadows
however the games GI term is far from perfect and can leave some areas quite dark so here you can control it
reduction in shadow strength can create an odd 90s style look where you can see a semblance of light leaking through to "fill in" for the shadow.
not a fan of it, and it's not accurate, but hey to each their own!

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_CLOTH
properties.comment: this does get used on characters but it's not common, default_lit

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_PREINTEGRATED_SKIN
properties.comment: (common on characters)

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_SUBSURFACE_PROFILE
properties.comment: (common on characters)

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_HAIR
properties.comment: (common on characters)

properties.name: DISABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS_FOR_EYE
properties.comment: (common on characters)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_FALLOFF
properties.comment:
another requested feature...
this is an added effect that will gradually "fade" contact shadows as it goes further out
this does have a bit of a perf hit with (extra instructions per iteration in the loop now)
I've done my best to optimize and keep it light, but it just requires more instructions to achieve
still, in the grand scheme of things this should be pretty light and enabled if you really want to mitigate some of shortcomings (atleast its not another texture sample)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_FALLOFF_CONTRAST
properties.comment:
this shapes the falloff
higher values = sharper/darker shadow further out
lower values = softer/lighter shadow further out

properties.name: SHADING_DEFAULT_LIT_LAMBERT
properties.comment:
this is the original shading model used for the game
its simple, and efficent, but not accurate
if you want to retain the original game shading turn this on

properties.name: SHADING_DEFAULT_LIT_BURLEY
properties.comment:
new shading model, little different but more accurate to diffuse shading in real life
visually it makes diffuse materials more "diffuse" and matte as it should caused by retro-reflection (when you look away from the light direction)
but for some artistically this might be undesirable

properties.name: SHADING_DEFAULT_LIT_OREN_NAYAR
properties.comment:
new shading model, little different but more accurate to diffuse shading in real life
similar to burley, visually it makes diffuse materials more "diffuse" and matte as it should caused by retro-reflection (when you look away from the light direction)
but for some artistically this might be undesirable

properties.name: ENABLE_MICRO_SHADOWS
properties.comment:
simulates micro-level shadowing on materials (using material ao) super cheap and performant! (from uncharted 4)
but this can lead to some materials/objects looking much darker than usual.
if this is not desired you can just disable to revert to (mostly) original shading

properties.name: ENABLE_MICRO_SHADOWS_SKIN
properties.comment:
applies microshadows to skin, generally shadowing terms should be mostly unified, however this can lead to an overly dark appearance characters in certain conditions and areas
I would leave it off if you desire characters to stay true to their original game shading

properties.name: ENABLE_MICRO_SHADOWS_HAIR
properties.comment:
applies microshadows to hair, generally shadowing terms should be mostly unified, however this can lead to an overly dark appearance characters in certain conditions and areas
I would leave it off if you desire characters to stay true to their original game shading

properties.name: MICRO_SHADOWS_STRENGTH
properties.comment:
requested feature for control over strength of shadows, the uncharted 4 micro shadow application at full intensity can be quite strong
leaving some places a little too dark when in direct sunlight, but here you have control over how strong it is

properties.name: APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT
properties.comment:
apply SSAO to the direct lighting for more contrast
NOTE: I don't recomend this, as it's not only physically in-accurate, but can create too much "shadowing" for things that are supposed to be in direct light
but... it's here if you prefer the look

properties.name: SSAO_POWER
properties.comment:
[APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT ONLY!] This only works if APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT is enabled!
this controls the "contrast" of the SSAO term when applied to direct light

properties.name: SSAO_BRIGHTNESS
properties.comment:
[APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT ONLY!] This only works if APPLY_SSAO_IN_DIRECT_LIGHT is enabled!
this controls the "brightness" of the SSAO term when applied to direct light, I suggest using this in tandem with SSAO_POWER

properties.name: RANDOM_ANIMATE_NOISE
properties.comment:
this changes the noise pattern every frame, which with Temporal Anti-Aliasing (or DLSS or anything related)
you want to do, that way samples change every frame and results get blended together over time for a better final apperance

properties.name: RANDOM_INTERLEAVED_GRADIENT_NOISE
properties.comment:
less "noisy" pattern, more stable and slightly better performing
NOTE 1: for animated noise, I recomend this as it's more stable

properties.name: RANDOM_BLUE_NOISE
properties.comment:
more "noisy" pattern, less stable and slightly worse perfoming
NOTE 1: for NON-animated noise, I recomend using this (because it's sample pattern has better distribution across a single frame)
NOTE 2: game uses this by default

properties.name: ENABLE_CONTACT_SHADOWS
properties.comment:
the main attraction, contact shadows!
in short it raymarches against the scene depth buffer to estimate shadows
significantly improves overall shadow quality

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_SAMPLES
properties.comment:
this directly controls the quality of the contact shadows, the more the better!
HIGHER VALUES: better quality shadows, less noise (more stable), and denser but expensive performance
LOWER VALUES: lower quality shadows, more noise (less stable), and lighter but cheaper performance

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_RAY_LENGTH
properties.comment:
this controls how far out the shadows go in screen space (and also can make shadows appear darker/denser or lighter depending on sample count)
HIGHER VALUES: shadows can reach farther, but can become noiser, and more expensive (more screen area)
LOWER VALUES: shadows don't reach as far, but can become more stable, and cheaper (less screen area)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_IMPROVED_THICKNESS
properties.comment: use a more accurate thickness hueristic that grows with the projected pixel footprint of the occluder, instead of a constant thickness for every sample

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_THICKNESS
properties.comment:
maximum assumed view-space thickness of an occluder.
with the improved path, the actual thickness starts at CONTACT_SHADOWS_MIN_THICKNESS and grows with the projected pixel footprint up to this cap.
with the legacy path this is the constant thickness used for every sample.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_MIN_THICKNESS
properties.comment: minimum thickness value of an occluder

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_PIXEL_THICKNESS_SCALE
properties.comment: multiplier for the view-space size of one pixel at the sampled depth.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_SELF_OCCLUSION_SKIP_STEPS
properties.comment:
receiver exclusion in march steps.
this prevents the first tested depth interval from overlapping the surface that launched the ray.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_GRAZING_EXTRA_SKIP_STEPS
properties.comment: extra exclusion at grazing light angles, where the ray remains close to the receiver plane for longer.

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_LOCAL_LIGHT_SHADOW_EXCLUSION_RADIUS_FACTOR
properties.comment:
FIX: this is a control specifically for local lights, where light sources placed inside geometry (that are supposed to emit light) would be occluded
this controls up to what point shadows will start for the shadow trace, this factor scales with the light radius
HIGHER VALUES: the shadows start much later, but too late and this can mean no contact shadows or shadowing for a majority of the light
LOWER VALUES: the shadows start much earlier, but too early and some meshes/light sources will still wind up being fully occluded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_BIAS
properties.comment:
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_BIAS_HAIR
properties.comment:
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces for hair specifically
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_NORMAL_BIAS
properties.comment:
this is a small bias factor to minimize contact shadow acne on sloped surfaces using surface normal
high values = reduced acne but can introduce visual issues where shadows appear less grounded
low values = potentially increased acne but keeps shadows grounded

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_EARLY_SKY_OUT
properties.comment:
OPTIMIZATION: this avoids calculating contact shadows for sky pixels
has no effect visually, but can save you quite a bit of frametime especially the more you look up :P
honestly no reason you should turn this off unless you want to suffer in vain...

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD
properties.comment:
OPTIMIZATION: this calculates contact shadows for every other pixel in a checkerboard like pattern that switches every frame
it saves a small bit of frametime, but does have a quality degredation with more visible shimmering at distances
disable if you want sharper true per-pixel contact shadows (at a bit of a perf hit)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION
properties.comment:
[CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD ONLY!] This only works if checkerboarding is enabled!
this tries to fill in the gaps intelligently during checkerboard rendering minimize holes where no shadow is calculated

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION_TYPE_MIN
properties.comment:
[CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD and CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION ONLY!] This only works if checkerboarding and quad reconstruction is enabled!
sharper | checks within the 2x2 checker block and if there is a shadow pixel it just copies it

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOW_CHECKERBOARD_QUAD_RECONSTRUCTION_TYPE_AVG
properties.comment: smoother | takes the values within the 2x2 checker block and averages them together for a slightly softer apperance

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_STRENGTH
properties.comment:
this was requested by quite a few people who wanted to control the strength of the shadows
physical accuracy is at 1.0 full power, and natrually global illumination (ambient, bounce, transmission light) fills in shadows
however the games GI term is far from perfect and can leave some areas quite dark so here you can control it
reduction in shadow strength can create an odd 90s style look where you can see a semblance of light leaking through to "fill in" for the shadow.
not a fan of it, and it's not accurate, but hey to each their own!

properties.comment: this does get used on characters but it's not common, default_lit

properties.comment:
another requested feature...
this is an added effect that will gradually "fade" contact shadows as it goes further out
this does have a bit of a perf hit with (extra instructions per iteration in the loop now)
I've done my best to optimize and keep it light, but it just requires more instructions to achieve
still, in the grand scheme of things this should be pretty light and enabled if you really want to mitigate some of shortcomings (atleast its not another texture sample)

properties.name: CONTACT_SHADOWS_FALLOFF_CONTRAST
properties.comment:
this shapes the falloff
higher values = sharper/darker shadow further out
lower values = softer/lighter shadow further out

properties.name: WATER_FOG_MAX_OPTICAL_DEPTH_CM
properties.comment:
unreal units are centimeters.
missing depth is treated as open water at this optical thickness instead of as an almost-clear black scene-buffer hole.

properties.name: VIGNETTE_ENABLED
properties.comment: original game vignettes, disabled by default because I hate how strong and wide they tend to be

properties.name: BLOOM_ENABLE
properties.comment: (BLOOM) game has bloom by default

properties.name: BLOOM_PHYSICAL
properties.comment:
(BLOOM) this changes the bloom compositing to be more "physically" accurate, making it more prevelant in some areas, but it's energy conserving
NOTE: if you want the original game bloom just disable BLOOM_PHYSICAL and BLOOM_ADDITIVE

properties.name: BLOOM_PHYSICAL_INTENSITY
properties.comment: (BLOOM) how strong the physical bloom compositing is, higher values means a more of a natrual "soft-focus" effect, lower values means much less soft focus effect (only very bright sources can still bloom)

properties.name: BLOOM_ADDITIVE
properties.comment: (BLOOM) this changes the bloom compositing to be more of a classic "additive"

properties.name: BLOOM_ADDITIVE_INTENSITY
properties.comment: (BLOOM) how strong the additive bloom compoisting is, higher values means a more intense bloom.

properties.name: SHARPEN_ENABLE
properties.comment: Applies a sample-free 2x2 quad sharpen to the tonemapped scene before UI compositing.

properties.name: SHARPEN_AMOUNT
properties.comment:
How strongly each pixel is separated from the average of the other three pixels in its quad.
0.0 disables sharpening while higher values produce a stronger effect.

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE
properties.comment:
(AUTO_EXPOSURE) automatic exposure, checks the overall exposure of the final image and adjusts the expousre so that it is not too bright or too dark.
unfortunately this is unusally expensive at the moment but because we are kinda limited... we just gotta deal with it for now
it's not perfect and will flicker occasionally, brightness changes are instantaneous also

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_GRID_X
properties.comment:
(AUTO_EXPOSURE) how many horizontal samples we take of the final image to gauge overall image exposure
more samples = more stable auto exposure (less flicker) but can be slower
less samples = less stable auto exposure (more flicker) but faster

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_GRID_Y
properties.comment:
(AUTO_EXPOSURE) how many vertical samples we take of the final image to gauge overall image exposure
more samples = more stable auto exposure (less flicker) but can be slower
less samples = less stable auto exposure (more flicker) but faster

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_MIDDLE_GRAY
properties.comment: (AUTO_EXPOSURE) this is the middle gray value that the auto exposure will try to achieve, this is a standard value for middle gray

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_STRENGTH
properties.comment: (AUTO_EXPOSURE) this is the strength of the auto exposure.

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_MIN_EV
properties.comment: (AUTO_EXPOSURE) this is the minimum (darkened) exposure value that the auto exposure can go to, this is in EV (exposure value) which is a logarithmic scale

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_MAX_EV
properties.comment: (AUTO_EXPOSURE) this is the maximum (brightened) exposure value that the auto exposure can go to, this is in EV (exposure value) which is a logarithmic scale

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_COMPENSATION_EV
properties.comment: (AUTO_EXPOSURE) this is the exposure compensation value that the auto exposure will apply to the final image, this is in EV (exposure value) which is a logarithmic scale

properties.name: AUTO_EXPOSURE_CENTER_FOCUS
properties.comment:
(AUTO_EXPOSURE) this controls how focused the grid points are when sampling the final image to determine the automatic exposure value
values closer to 1.0 are focused towards the center of the screen
values closer to 0.0 are more spread out across the entire screen

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_BRIGHTNESS_EV
properties.comment:
how bright the image is
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_CONTRAST
properties.comment:
how much contrast the image has
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_CONTRAST_PIVOT
properties.comment:
the pivot point for the contrast adjustment, this is the value that the contrast adjustment will be centered around
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_SATURATION
properties.comment:
how much saturation the image has
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_VIBRANCE
properties.comment:
how much vibrance the image has, this is a more subtle saturation adjustment that only affects the less saturated colors
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_TINT_COLOR
properties.comment:
how much tint the image has, this is a color adjustment that shifts the overall color balance of the image
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_TINT_FACTOR
properties.comment:
how much tint the image has, this is a color adjustment that shifts the overall color balance of the image
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_GAMMA
properties.comment:
how much gamma the image has, this functions almost like a contrast adjustment (but think of it as a "soft" contrast adjustment)
higher values make for a brighter/less contrasty image
lower values make for a darker/more contrasty image
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_LIFT
properties.comment:
how much lift the image has, this is a color adjustment that shifts the overall color balance of the image
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: ADJUSTMENT_GAIN
properties.comment:
how much gain the image has, this is a color adjustment that shifts the overall color balance of the image
(applied before tonemap)

properties.name: TONEMAP_PRESERVE_COLOR_GRADE
properties.comment:
NOTE: this only applies if a tonemap is enabled
I would recomend leaving this on, but this very accurately preserves the original game color grade when applying a new tonemap
because in the original game the tonemapping is baked into the LUTs that get used, good for performance but not for flexibility

properties.name: TONEMAP_NONE

raw untonemapped framebuffer to screen with srgb conversion
(NOTE: only one tonemap can be active at a time)

properties.name: TONEMAP_GRAN_TURISMO_7

personal favorite, not 'filmic' but gives a much more natrual tonal and color response (ironically this matches more closely to the tonal response in the pre-rendered cutscenes)
(NOTE: only one tonemap can be active at a time)

properties.name: DISABLE_SSR
properties.comment:
this completely disables the entire SSR pass and effectively makes it return no data (performant)
if you want no SSR you can enable this

properties.name: RANDOM_ANIMATE_NOISE
properties.comment:
this changes the noise pattern every frame, which with Temporal Anti-Aliasing (or DLSS or anything related)
you want to do this, that way samples change every frame and results get blended together over time for a better final apperance

properties.name: RANDOM_BLUE_NOISE
properties.comment: this is used by the game by default, recomended

properties.name: RANDOM_WHITE_NOISE
properties.comment: this is a non-texture based, more random than blue noise but can look worse because of that

properties.name: ENABLE_SSR_ROUGHNESS
properties.comment:
factors in surface roughness for much better/higher quality reflections
this does make the SSR a little more expensive and introduces more noise (more randomness = less coherence)
but overall reflections are higher quality, and respect the material properties within the scene (the original does not)

properties.name: SSR_RAY_COUNT
properties.comment:
number of independent reflection rays traced per pixel
expensive, but if you want to reduce the noise from ENABLE_SSR_ROUGHNESS this is one way to control it

properties.name: SSR_OVERRIDE_STEP_COUNT
properties.comment:
disabled by default, but enabling this allows you to set the sample count in regards to the raymarch
higher quality means less artifacts

properties.name: SSR_STEP_COUNT
properties.comment: how many raymarching steps we do for the SSR, higher steps mean better quality/accuracy but more expensive

properties.name: SSR_DEPTH_THICKNESS_MULTIPLIER
properties.comment:
disabled by default, but this allows you to control the thickness factor in regards to the raymarching
smaller values meanse less artifacts, but reflections appear less "full"

properties.name: WATER_WAVE_SCALE_A_MULTIPLIER
properties.comment: increase the UV tiling for water waves since on average they are way to large scale

properties.name: WATER_WAVE_FLOW_MAP_SPEED_MULTIPLER
properties.comment: slow speed down a bit because most water sources in the game move TOO fast

properties.name: WATER_MAX_INDIRECT_ENERGY_SCALE
properties.comment:
bound energy matching and the final pre-exposed HDR result so invalid or
near-singular inputs cannot turn into bloom-amplified fireflies.
